name: Chinese · Phrases · Shopping and paying
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.note: The basic price question, anywhere.
Shop staff call this as you walk in — no reply needed.
Polite brush-off when staff ask what you need.
Bargaining at markets and small shops; not in malls or chains.
Reacting to a price, often as the first move in bargaining.
Asking the total at the till.

entries.back: Can I pay by QR code?
entries.note: Most places take WeChat Pay or Alipay by scanning a code.
Staff line asking how you'll pay.
Staff line at the till; bags usually cost a little extra.
Asking in a clothes shop.

entries.reading: yǒu dà yī hào de ma？
entries.back: Do you have this one size up?
entries.note: Use 小一号 for a size down.

entries.back: Does it come in other colours?
entries.note: Asking for other options.

entries.reading: zhè bù shì wǒ de chǐmǎ
entries.note: After trying something on, or when handed the wrong size.
Deciding what to buy.
Soft way to leave without buying.
Pointing at something behind the counter.
Market version of the price question, e.g. for fruit sold by weight.
Card isn't taken everywhere; worth asking first.
Paying cash with a big note.
Asking about returns before or after buying.

entries.reading: néng bāng wǒ bāo qǐlai ma？
entries.back: Could you wrap it up for me?
entries.note: For gifts or fragile things.

entries.back: Do you have a membership card?
entries.note: Staff line at the till; just say 没有 if you don't.

entries.term: 不好意思，请问鸡蛋在哪儿？
entries.reading: bù hǎoyìsi， qǐngwèn jīdàn zài nǎr？
entries.back: Excuse me, where are the eggs?
entries.note: Asking staff in a supermarket; swap in any item.

entries.back: Is there a supermarket near here?
entries.note: Asking a local or hotel staff.
Checking opening hours.
Commenting while shopping with a friend.

entries.reading: wǒ wǎn diǎn zài lái ná
entries.back: I'll come back for it later.
entries.note: When an item needs altering or you'll pick it up later.

entries.reading: huílai de lùshang mǎi diǎn niúnǎi
entries.back: Grab some milk on your way back.
entries.note: Errand request to family.

entries.reading: bāng wǒ mǎi diǎn língshí ba
entries.back: Get me some snacks, would you?
entries.note: Asking a friend heading to the shop.
发票 is the official receipt, needed for work expenses.
